links.outcome: Rate of escalation on planning tasks with proven-incompatible dose goals (overlap contradictions)
links.effect: Despite 95.4% and 92.1% decision accuracy, the script with LLM review and the full agent escalated only 50% (95% CI 25-75%) and 25% (10-40%) of overlap contradictions.
links.quote: With Terra, the script preceded by an LLM review and the full agent had decision accuracies of 95.4% and 92.1%, respectively, yet escalated only 50% (95% confidence interval, 25-75%) and 25% (10-40%) of overlap contradictions, which required arithmetic on the anatomy.

links.outcome: Whether the clinical agent could stop or request review when a goal repeatedly failed
links.effect: In four SAGE runs one goal failed at every attempt; the agent identified it in every reply but had no action for stopping.
links.quote: In four SAGE runs, one goal failed at every attempt; the agent identified it in every reply but had no action for stopping.

unlisted_practices: Evaluating planning agents on decision correctness (submit vs. request review) using known-answer tasks, not only dose outcomes
Comparing the achieved plan against a stored feasible reference plan to detect missed hard goals

screen.reason: The study develops and applies a benchmark (OpenGray) to evaluate the decision-making and safety/escalation actions of LLM-based radiotherapy planning agents.
